findings.trigger_condition: The edge stream contains two equal values where one is hashable and the other is not — concretely a set and an equal frozenset ({1} == frozenset({1}) is True) — used as node/dependency values, especially when the same logical node appears in both edge positions (self-dependency or mutual pair).
findings.root_cause: _id_of maintains two disjoint identity registries: hashable values go through hash_buckets (line 42) and unhashable values through a separate unhashable_ids/unhashable_nodes linear list (lines 43-52). Equality is only ever compared against entries of the same registry, so one logical node that is representable in both registries (set vs frozenset) is split into two distinct ids. Edge dedup (seen_edges of id pairs, line 72), indegree counting, and cycle detection all operate on the split ids.
findings.impact: All reproduced empirically: (1) Missed real cycle: dependency_layers([({1}, frozenset({1}))]) returns [[frozenset({1})], [{1}]] instead of raising DependencyCycleError, although the node equals its own dependency (a real directed self-cycle) — violates the requirement to raise for real cycles. (2) False cycle with wrong error payload: dependency_layers([({1}, frozenset({1})), (frozenset({1}), {1})]) raises DependencyCycleError reporting two nodes for what is a single self-dependent node. (3) Broken layering and dedup: dependency_layers([('a', frozenset({1})), ({1}, 'b')]) returns [[frozenset({1}), 'b'], ['a', {1}]] — 'a' lands in the same layer as its equal dependency, violating 'dependencies in earlier layers than dependents'; and dependency_layers([('a', {1}), ('a', frozenset({1}))]) returns [[{1}, frozenset({1})], ['a']], emitting the same logical node twice in one layer, violating edge deduplication.
findings.suggested_validation: Add tests: dependency_layers([({1}, frozenset({1}))]) must raise DependencyCycleError; [('a', {1}), ('a', frozenset({1}))] must yield exactly one dependency node; [('a', frozenset({1})), ({1}, 'b')] must place 'b' before the merged node before 'a'. Fix by using a single equality-based registry: on TypeError from hash, look the value up in the same bucket structure via a fallback path (or keep one shared list consulted for every lookup) so equal values map to one id regardless of hashability.

findings.trigger_condition: Edge streams with many distinct unhashable node values (e.g. lists as nodes): every lookup for a new unhashable value scans all previously registered unhashable values.
findings.root_cause: The unhashable fallback in _id_of performs an O(U) linear scan (line 44) per registration/lookup, giving O(U^2) total time for U unhashable nodes; there is no hash-partitioning or indexed structure on the fallback path (the hashable path is fine).
findings.impact: Quadratic slowdown on large unhashable graphs, measured: n=500 -> 0.011s, n=1000 -> 0.040s, n=2000 -> 0.159s (clean 4x per doubling). Extrapolated, a 100k-node unhashable chain takes hundreds of seconds. The spec's 'handle very deep acyclic inputs' scale expectation is only met for hashable nodes; correctness is unaffected.
findings.suggested_validation: Time dependency_layers on list-node chains of n=10000 vs n=20000 and assert the ratio is well under 3x (near-linear). Fix by partitioning unhashable values under a cheap derived key (e.g. type or repr prefix) before the equality scan, or by mapping unhashable values through a canonical wrapper (e.g. a tuple (type-tag, repr)) into the existing hash_buckets structure with an equality confirmation step.
